Part 2 of 3

Undertone

Even two people with the exact same skin depth can look completely different in the same foundation — because of undertone. It's the subtle hue beneath your skin's surface that determines whether a shade looks natural or off.

Cool pink · rosy · red
Neutral balanced · even
Warm golden · yellow · olive

A foundation matched only on depth but wrong in undertone will look ashy, orange, or pink. Getting this right is what makes your shade truly invisible on skin.

Tip

Answer each question based on what naturally looks best on you — not what you think your undertone "should" be. Trust your first instinct.

Part 3 of 3

Saturation

Saturation is the intensity of color in your skin — how vivid or muted it appears. It's the difference between a foundation that looks flat and chalky versus one that looks alive and dimensional.

Olive muted · soft · grey-green
Medium balanced · neither extreme
Peach bright · vivid · warm flush

Without accounting for saturation, even a perfect depth and undertone match can look wrong — too grey and flat, or too loud and orange. These next questions help us get the color intensity exactly right.

Tip

Think about how your bare skin looks in natural daylight — not after a long day or under artificial light.
